stories.title: IndiGo flight diverted to Lucknow after pilot reported minimum fuel
stories.summary: An IndiGo flight from Bhubaneswar to Varanasi was diverted to Lucknow after the pilot reported minimum fuel. While other aircraft were permitted to land at Varanasi, the IndiGo flight was denied clearance by air traffic control. Passengers eventually disembarked after initially refusing to leave the aircraft.

stories.title: IndiGo flight diverted to Lucknow after minimum fuel alert, to leave for Varanasi at 9am
stories.summary: LUCKNOW: An IndiGo flight carrying 175 passengers and six crew members from Bhubaneswar to Varanasi was diverted to Lucknow on Friday night after the pilot reported minimum fuel, according to a source. The flight is now scheduled to depart for Varanasi at 9am on Saturday. Passengers initially hesitated to deboard

stories.title: IndiGo to resume operations to Jeddah and Madinah
stories.summary: IndiGo will resume select flights between India and the Saudi Arabian cities of Jeddah and Madinah. The airline previously suspended these services due to regional security concerns. Flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam remain cancelled until December 7 as the airline assesses the situation.

stories.title: Belagavi airport terminal nears completion
stories.summary: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu announced the new terminal at Belagavi Airport is 99.8 percent complete. The facility covers 16,400 square metres and includes four aerobridges. The project aims to enhance passenger experience and infrastructure, though the final 0.2 percent remains pending.

stories.title: Noida International Airport begins commercial operations
stories.summary: Noida International Airport has officially commenced operations, welcoming its first scheduled flight from Lucknow. Developed by Zurich Airport Limited, the facility aims to expand connectivity across the National Capital Region. The airport serves as a new gateway for northern India, with regular services to Bengaluru now active.

stories.title: Navi Mumbai airport serves 4 million passengers
stories.summary: Navi Mumbai International Airport has recorded over 4 million passengers in less than 11 months of operation. Data shows domestic travellers account for nearly all traffic, with a peak of 27,000 passengers on November 19. The airport reaches its first anniversary on December 25.

stories.title: Cathay Cargo shifts Mumbai freighter operations to Navi Mumbai
stories.summary: Cathay Cargo has moved its Mumbai freighter operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport. The carrier will operate three weekly flights to its Hong Kong hub using Boeing 747-400ERF and 747-8F aircraft. The move provides main-deck capacity for heavy cargo shipments to international markets.

stories.title: IndiGo adds daily flights to Udaipur
stories.summary: IndiGo has announced new daily non-stop flights to Udaipur from Noida and Navi Mumbai. The Noida route begins October 25, with the Navi Mumbai service following on November 15. The expansion aims to provide additional travel options for business and leisure passengers in southern Rajasthan.

stories.title: IndiGo launches daily Pune to Bhubaneswar flights
stories.summary: IndiGo will launch daily non-stop flights between Pune and Bhubaneswar starting October 25. The route will be operated by an Airbus A320, marking the airline's 15th destination served from Bhubaneswar. The service is intended to facilitate travel for professionals, students, and leisure passengers.

stories.title: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy
stories.summary: Norwegian budget airline Norse Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy after halting all flights and ticket sales. The board of directors concluded there was no longer a basis for continued operations. The carrier, founded in 2021, had provided long-haul flights between Europe, Asia, and the United States.

Budget airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy in Europe after failing to secure funding

It’s the latest transport chaos to face passengers, who already have filed so many complaints against airlines this

The Norwegian long-haul carrier said it remains in talks with investors about a possible takeover

stories.title: Boeing wins $2.82 billion order for 15 KC-46 tankers
stories.summary: The US Air Force has awarded Boeing a $2.82 billion contract for 15 KC-46A Pegasus tankers, completing the original 2011 deal. The Pentagon expects work to run through June 2030. The Air Force paid $2.47 billion for the same number of aircraft last year.

stories.title: Aeroméxico to revamp B787 fleet with new Premier One suites
stories.summary: Aeroméxico will revamp its Boeing 787 fleet to provide a more personalized experience, featuring a 70 percent expansion in premium seat capacity. The project will reduce total seat counts on its B787-9 and B787-8 aircraft. The airline is currently finalizing the cabin refresh design.

stories.title: Air Corsica expands A320 fleet
stories.summary: Air Corsica plans to add eight Airbus A320s to its fleet by March 2028. CEO Pierre Muracciole stated the airline has board approval to expand beyond its core public service obligation routes. The carrier is now looking toward new intra-European services.

stories.title: Xiamen Airlines signals narrowbody fleet refresh with 50 Boeing 737 MAX jets
stories.summary: Xiamen Airlines is buying 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft in a deal valued at $7.4 billion at list prices. The jets are scheduled for delivery between 2031 and 2034. Parent company China Southern Airlines noted that Boeing offered a significant discount on the order.

stories.title: Pictet Asset Management visits Beta Technologies
stories.summary: Investment managers from Pictet Asset Management flew in an electric aircraft while visiting Beta Technologies in Vermont. The visit highlighted the investment case for electric aviation, which relies on upcoming FAA certification milestones and the build-out of charging infrastructure. The firm evaluates hundreds of companies annually.

stories.title: Netherlands plans order for two more NH90 helicopters
stories.summary: The Netherlands is planning to acquire two additional NHIndustries NH90 helicopters. The move utilizes options from an order for three aircraft placed last year. Documents from the Defense Ministry indicate the country intended to exercise these options since the initial purchase.

stories.title: Taneja Aerospace completes acquisition of TAAL Precision Products
stories.summary: Taneja Aerospace and Aviation has finalized the acquisition of TAAL Precision Products, making it a wholly owned subsidiary. The transaction concluded in late November 2026. The company did not disclose the financial consideration for the consolidation of its component manufacturing capacity.

stories.title: ANA Holdings establishes pilot training company with JGAS
stories.summary: ANA Holdings and Japan General Aviation Service have founded ANA Next Aviation to centralize basic flight training in Japan. The company was formed with ten million yen in capital and is 70 percent owned by ANA. The move addresses forecasts of significant pilot retirements.

stories.title: ANA HOLDINGS establishes Japan's only airline-affiliated pilot training company, ANA Next Aviation - Air Cargo Week
EASA orders emergency Airbus H160 cockpit window checks
stories.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency has ordered emergency inspections of Airbus H160-B helicopters. An assembly-line check revealed that cockpit escape windows could detach during flight. Operators must inspect all serial numbers within 10 flight hours and correct any identified issues before further operation.

stories.title: FAA orders B757 checks over fuselage cracking
stories.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration has issued an order regarding fuselage cracking on Boeing 757 aircraft. The directive follows ongoing maintenance requirements for the aging fleet. The FAA maintains extensive databases tracking over 110,000 aircraft to support such safety oversight and regulatory compliance.

stories.title: Unexpected stall behavior prompts Piper PA-44 airworthiness concern
stories.summary: The FAA issued an airworthiness concern sheet after reports of unexpected roll behavior in Piper PA-44 Seminoles during stall maneuvers. The aircraft experienced rolls of 60 degrees, significantly exceeding the expected 15-degree limit. The issue may be more likely to occur with multiple people on board.

stories.title: FAA proposes expanded airworthiness directive for Dassault Falcon jets
stories.summary: The FAA has proposed expanding an airworthiness directive for certain Dassault Falcon business jets. The proposal addresses concerns that improperly heat-treated titanium screws could fail and reduce structural integrity. The agency routinely updates these directives to align with foreign authority revisions.

stories.title: Corporate jets are being redacted from the FAA registry
stories.summary: Since March 2025, the FAA has allowed private aircraft owners to request the redaction of personal details from public databases. The process stems from the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024. It remains unclear whether corporate entities qualify for the same privacy protections as individuals.

stories.title: FAA proposes stricter helicopter maintenance
stories.summary: The FAA has proposed new maintenance requirements for several Airbus helicopter models to prevent critical component failures. The proposal would replace existing directives with more restrictive safety limitations. The agency is currently accepting feedback regarding implementation timelines and potential operational costs for commercial operators.

stories.title: FAA proposes expanded Falcon jet inspections
stories.summary: The FAA is seeking input by January 4 on a proposal to expand inspections for Dassault Falcon 7X, 900EX, and 2000EX jets. The agency estimates compliance costs of $1.13 million across 52 U.S.-registered aircraft. The directive targets potentially faulty titanium screws that could compromise structural integrity.

stories.title: India updates aviation rulebook with Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam 2026
stories.summary: India has introduced the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam 2026 to update its regulatory framework for civil aviation. The number of operational airports in the country has grown from 74 in 2014 to 166 as of October 2026. The new rules aim to keep pace with evolving aircraft technology.

stories.title: Aviation expert calls for independent safety board in India
stories.summary: Former pilot Minoo Wadia has called for a fundamental overhaul of India's Directorate General of Civil Aviation. He advocates for the creation of an independent safety board to improve oversight. The Federation of Indian Pilots has reportedly raised these structural concerns with the government for several decades.

stories.title: Southwest Airlines pilot pay remains tied to seniority
stories.summary: Southwest Airlines does not use a separate pay scale for pilots flying the Boeing 737 MAX. Instead, pay is determined by a system based on seat position and seniority. The final amount depends on scheduling practices and extra flights, as the airline operates only one aircraft type.

Lufthansa balances hub job cuts with pilot hiring
stories.summary: Lufthansa faces proposals to cut 1,000 hub jobs at Frankfurt and Munich while simultaneously offering to hire 1,000 new pilots by 2033. The airline describes these as separate efforts to slim down one area while bolstering another. The math is balanced, if not the workforce.

stories.title: AirAsia Philippines faces pilot strike over layoffs
stories.summary: AirAsia Philippines says operations remain normal despite the retrenchment of 90 pilots. The AirAsia Philippines Pilots Union filed a notice of strike on 26 November to protest the layoffs and seek formal recognition. The airline maintains that all domestic and international flights will continue to operate as scheduled.

stories.title: AirAsia Philippines faces potential disruption from pilot strike
stories.summary: AirAsia Philippines is preparing for a potential strike as the pilots union challenges the retrenchment of 90 captains and first officers. The move is part of a wider workforce reduction affecting approximately 250 employees. The union is currently seeking formal recognition from the airline.

ANA Holdings launches pilot training subsidiary
stories.summary: ANA Holdings has established ANA Next Aviation to manage pilot training in partnership with Japan General Aviation Service. The company aims to secure a stable supply of flight crew amid expectations of a growing pilot shortage in Japan. The initiative began operations on 31 October 2026.

stories.title: Kothari Industrial signs drone training agreements
stories.summary: Kothari Industrial has entered into two memorandums of understanding focused on drone pilot training and UAV research and development. The company is expanding its operational focus into commercial agricultural drones and associated skilling infrastructure.

stories.title: Kothari Industrial partners with engineering college for drone training
stories.summary: Kothari Industrial Corporation has partnered with Thiagarajar College of Engineering for drone pilot training and UAV research in Tamil Nadu. The initiative is part of the company's broader focus on commercial agricultural drones and skilling infrastructure. The agreement details remain subject to independent verification.
